Managed EV charging, for both price-responsive and DLC mechanisms, is also fixed in the day- ahead and real-time stages. The real-time stage always sees the actual managed profile, with unit commitment and pumped hydropower storage schedules fixed as in the unmanaged scenario. Scenario foresight differences result from whether the unit commitment and pumped hydropower storage schedules were computed in a day-ahead run with the same (actual managed) EV charging load profile (perfect-foresight) or in the unmanaged day-ahead run (no-foresight). While the price-responsive managed profiles (TOU and RTP) are computed by dispatching individual vehicle charging flexibility against prices using dsgrid-flex, DLC managed profiles are computed using a PLEXOS regional day-ahead run (Stage 0). This regional Stage 0 run is formulated to limit the computational complexity of dispatching aggregate EVMC, especially for within-week flexibility. (DLC is always assumed to operate under perfect-foresight conditions, that is, directly coordinated with supply.) For price-responsive mechanisms we apply a $1/(MW/h) ramping penalty to 100-vehicle batches of aggregated price-responsive EVMC to encourage flatter responses across equal-cost hours. This method of response flattening is more effective for TOU, which has long periods of equal prices, than for RTP, in which prices vary hourly and often by more than $1/MWh. The inclusion of this ramping penalty is important for interpreting reduced TOU ramp rate results such as those in Figure 4. Both sets of dispatch results are aggregated to the load region level before being passed to PLEXOS to run the nodal day-ahead (Stage 1) and real-time (Stage 2) models. The county to load region mapping (for price-responsive dispatch of individual vehicles, each of which is located in a single New England county) is determined by assigning each county to the nearest PLEXOS load node, each of which is assigned to a single load region.
